title: Internal-Hom tensor criterion for lisse adic cohomology
statement:
Let $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, let $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite inside a fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$, and let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. Use the raw rationalized category $D^b_c(T,E)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] or its common-finite-stage category $D^b_c(T,\Qlb)$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]; write $\Lambda$ for the chosen field stage. Tensor, unit $\Lambda_T$ and internal Hom are the completed-integral, rationalized and common-stage operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and cohomology is the standard constructible cohomology. Lisse in the heart means pro-etale locally a finite direct sum of the coefficient unit, with rank zero and varying local rank allowed, as in [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization].

For $K\in D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$ put $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_T(K,\Lambda_T)$, and suppose $K^\vee$ belongs to this category. Suppose that for every $N\in D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$ the canonical evaluation comparison
$$c_{K,N}:K^\vee\otimes^L N\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_T(K,N)$$
is an isomorphism, where $c_{K,N}$ is the tensor--Hom transpose of $K^\vee\otimes^L N\otimes^L K\to N$ obtained from evaluation and symmetry. Then every $\mathcal H^j(K)$, $j\in\mathbf Z$, is lisse of finite rank. No lisse integral lattice on all of $T$ is assumed.

source.place: Definition 3.3 (lisse = dualizable), Theorem 6.2(2), Corollary 6.3 and Corollary 6.11; comparison Theorem 7.7 and Lemma 7.9. Raw rationalization: Bhatt--Scholze Proposition 6.8.14(2), rather than an assumed Karoubi completion. The evaluation-comparison hypothesis is the closed-monoidal criterion for dualizability; this is an agent formulation of their consequence.

proof.text:
Put $\mathcal C=D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$, $D=K^\vee$ and let $e:D\otimes K\to\mathbf1$ be evaluation. For $A,N\in\mathcal C$, compose symmetry $N\otimes D\cong D\otimes N$, the assumed $c_{K,N}$, and the tensor--Hom transpose bijection of [lem-coef-completed-tensor-hom-transpose]. This gives bijections $\Phi_{A,N}:\operatorname{Hom}(A,N\otimes D)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A\otimes K,N)$ with formula $f\mapsto(1_N\otimes e)(f\otimes1_K)$, by the specified transpose defining $c_{K,N}$. At the common stage, represent all objects and arrows at a finite field and take the filtered colimit of the rational bijections. This uses the common-stage operation on arrows of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the representative equivalence relation of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category].

Set $\eta=\Phi_{\mathbf1,K}^{-1}(1_K):\mathbf1\to K\otimes D$. Its defining equation is the first triangle $(1_K\otimes e)(\eta\otimes1_K)=1_K$. For $r=(e\otimes1_D)(1_D\otimes\eta):D\to D$, tensor bifunctoriality gives
$$\Phi_{D,\mathbf1}(r)=e(r\otimes1_K)=e\bigl(1_D\otimes[(1_K\otimes e)(\eta\otimes1_K)]\bigr)=e=\Phi_{D,\mathbf1}(1_D).$$
Here associators and unitors are suppressed, and the middle equality interchanges the evaluations on the two disjoint $D\otimes K$ factors. Injectivity yields $r=1_D$, the second triangle. Thus $K,D,e,\eta$ are a dual pair in the given category, without choosing an integral lisse lattice.

source.place: Definition 3.3(1): establish the dualizability input from the canonical evaluation comparisons

proof.text: If $\Lambda=E$, retain this dual pair at the given field stage. If $\Lambda=\Qlb$, choose a common finite field $F$ over which $K,D,e,\eta$ and the unit are represented. This is possible from the object-and-arrow construction of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. The completed operations and their scalar comparisons in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] represent the two composites in the triangle identities at finite fields as well. Equality of two representatives in the pair category means equality after some further finite coefficient extension. Choose one such extension for each of the two triangle identities and then their compositum. At that enlarged $F$ both identities hold. Consequently $K$ is represented by a finite-stage complex $K_F$ with an actual dual pair in the raw rationalized category at $F$. This argument descends only finitely many objects, arrows and equalities, rather than a condition quantified over all test complexes. When the pair category uses the PBC finite-stage model, identify its objects and arrows with the framework raw rationalization by [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison]. This comparison is the identity on the common integral category and on localized Hom groups; the products appearing here use the same completed integral operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Thus $K_F$ and its displayed duality maps are in the finite-stage model used in Step 3.

source.place: Lemma 7.9: finite-stage interpretation; finite dual-pair data descend directly by the pair-category equivalence relation

proof.text: Write $F$ for the field from Step 2 (or $E$ in the finite-stage case), put $B_T=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,T}$ and $F_T=B_T[1/\varpi_F]$, and use $J_{T,F}$ of [lem-zl-rational-realization-tensor-comparison]. The finite-stage category identification [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] and the equivalence [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] give its exact realization into the ambient derived category of $F_T$-module sheaves. The latter statement identifies $F_T$ with the continuous coefficient sheaf. Apply $J_{T,F}$ to $e,\eta$ and insert the tensor and unit comparisons of [lem-zl-rational-realization-tensor-comparison]. Since these comparisons commute with associators and unitors, each realized triangle composite is the image of the corresponding identity in Step 2, hence is an identity. Thus $J_{T,F}(K_F)$ is dualizable for ordinary derived tensor over $F_T$, in the full ambient derived category. This uses only tensor and unit compatibility, without assuming an internal-Hom comparison.

The condensed coefficient ring $\underline F(S)=C(S,F)$ is the ring of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Its underlying ring is the field $F$. Every finitely presented $F$-module is finite free, so this ring is regular coherent; every $F$-module $C(S,F)$ is flat, by choosing a vector-space basis. Hence the two t-admissibility hypotheses in [lem-zl-t-admissible-dualizable-truncations] hold. The finite affine cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], together with [lem-sfb-finite-type-noetherian-spectrum] applied to $\operatorname{Spec}k$, makes $|T|$ noetherian: an ascending open chain stabilizes on each of finitely many affine charts and hence stabilizes globally. By [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components], $T$ has finitely many irreducible components. Apply [lem-zl-t-admissible-dualizable-truncations] to the dualizable complex of Step 3. Each $\mathcal H^j(J_{T,F}K_F)$ is pro-etale locally $F_T\otimes_{\underline F}\underline N$ for some finitely presented $F$-vector space $N$. Choosing a finite basis of $N$ identifies this sheaf with $F_T^{\oplus r}$, including $r=0$. The theorem permits a different $N$ on each cover member, so it imposes no constant-rank condition across components.

source.place: Definition 6.1, Theorem 6.2(2), and Corollaries 6.3 and 6.11(1) specialized to the finite coefficient field

proof.text: The identity-on-integral-objects comparison [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] preserves integral cohomology and its localized standard pair. The t-exact realization [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] therefore identifies $J_{T,F}(\mathcal H^jK_F)$ with $\mathcal H^j(J_{T,F}K_F)$. Step 4 puts this sheaf in the local finite free essential image specified by [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization]. The realization in that statement is the same coefficient extension on integral representatives and localized morphisms, so its full faithfulness identifies $\mathcal H^jK_F$ with a lisse object of the rational constructible heart. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, [prop-constructible-truncations] says that the common-stage truncations commute with finite scalar extension; hence $\mathcal H^jK$ is the common-stage image of $\mathcal H^jK_F$. The final common-stage clause of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] preserves its local finite free bases and finite ranks. This proves the conclusion for every $j\in\mathbf Z$ at both coefficient stages.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2); lisse realization and common-stage truncation conventions
